executive_summary.question: What punishment applies to abetment of an offence when the Sanhita makes no express provision for punishing that specific abetment?
executive_summary.generated_answer:
When the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 contains **no express provision** for punishing a particular act of abetment, the law supplies a default punishment that depends on whether the abetted act was actually carried out and on the nature of the offence: | Situation | Default punishment (no express provision for abetment) | Source | |-----------|-----------------------------------------------|--------| | **The act abetted is committed in consequence of the abetment** | The abettor receives **the same punishment as the offence** that was abetted. | § 49 – “Whoever abets any offence shall … be punished with the punishment provided for the offence.”【e3cfd376-1174-46eb-9573-2b6cafe0dbc6】 | | **The offence is *not* committed** (abetment unsuccessful) | • If the offence is punishable with **death or imprisonment for life**: imprisonment of either description for a term **up to seven years**, and also liable to fine;
• If, in consequence of the abetment, any hurt is caused to a person: imprisonment of either description for a term **up to fourteen years**, and also liable to fine. | § 55 – “Whoever abets the commission of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life … be punished with imprisonment … which may extend to seven years … and shall also be liable to fine; and if any act … which causes hurt … be done … imprisonment … which may extend to fourteen years … and shall also be liable to fine.”【320c1526-fed5-4985-ae85-e16910f24ab6】 | | **The offence is punishable with imprisonment (but not death or life)** and is not committed | Imprisonment of any description provided for that offence for a term **up to one‑fourth of the longest term** prescribed for the offence (or **up to one‑half** if the abettor or the person abetted is a public servant whose duty is to prevent such offence), **with or without fine**. | § 56 – “Whoever abets an offence punishable with imprisonment … be punished with imprisonment … for a term which may extend to one‑fourth part of the longest term …; or with such fine …; and if the abettor … is a public servant … imprisonment … for a term which may extend to one‑half of the longest term … or with such fine ….”【a90a5461-96e5-4ff3-b754-c6e6c504fe4e】 | **In short:** - If the abetted act actually occurs, the abettor is punished exactly as if they had committed the offence themselves. - If the abetted act does **not** occur, the punishment falls back on a graduated scale: up to seven years (or fourteen years if hurt results) for offences attracting death or life imprisonment, and up to one‑fourth (or one‑half for public servants) of the maximum imprisonment term for other imprisonable offences, with the possibility of a fine in each case. These rules are drawn from sections 49, 55, and 56 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

evidence_analysis.claim_text: If the act abetted is committed in consequence of the abetment, the abettor receives the same punishment as the offence that was abetted.

evidence_analysis.claim_text: Section 49 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 provides that "Whoever abets any offence shall be punished with the punishment provided for the offence."

If the offence is not committed and the offence is punishable with death or imprisonment for life, the abettor is punished with imprisonment of either description for a term up to seven years and also liable to fine.
evidence_analysis.supporting_evidence:

imprisonment for life, shall, if that offence be not committed in consequence of the abetment,
and no express provision is made under this Sanhita for the punishment of such abetment, be
punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven
years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if any act for which the abettor is liable in consequence
of the abetment, and which causes hurt to any person, is done, the abettor shall be liable to
imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to fourteen years, and shall
also be liable to fine.

evidence_analysis.claim_text: If the offence is not committed and, in consequence of the abetment, any hurt is caused to a person, the abettor is punished with imprisonment of either description for a term up to fourteen years and also liable to fine.
evidence_analysis.supporting_evidence:

would have been subject to the punishment of death or imprisonment for life.Therefore, Ais

evidence_analysis.claim_text: Section 55 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 provides that "Whoever abets the commission of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine; and if any act which causes hurt is done, imprisonment may extend to fourteen years and shall also be liable to fine."

If the offence is not committed and the offence is punishable with imprisonment (but not death or life), the abettor is punished with imprisonment of any description provided for that offence for a term up to one-fourth of the longest term prescribed for the offence, with or without fine.

If the offence is not committed, the offence is punishable with imprisonment (but not death or life), and the abettor or the person abetted is a public servant whose duty is to prevent such offence, the abettor is punished with imprisonment of any description provided for that offence for a term up to one-half of the longest term prescribed for the offence, with or without fine.

Section 56 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 provides that "Whoever abets an offence punishable with imprisonment shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one-fourth part of the longest term, or with such fine; and if the abettor is a public servant, imprisonment may extend to one-half of the longest term or with such fine."
evidence_analysis.supporting_evidence:

longest term provided for that offence; or with such fine as is provided for that offence, or
with both; and if the abettor or the person abetted is a public servant, whose duty it is to
prevent the commission of such offence, the abettor shall be punished with imprisonment of
any description provided for that offence, for a term which may extend to one-half of the
longest term provided for that offence, or with such fine as is provided for the offence, or
with both.
